test_title: PYST 4: SSC Stenographer - Reasoning (Held On:18 Nov 2022 Shift 1)
subject: reasoning
question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All beards are nails.

Some nails are rings.

All rings are pendants.

**Conclusions:**

I. All rings can never be nails.

II. Some beards are rings.

III. Some nails are pendants.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

solution:
Given Statements:

All beards are nails.

Some nails are rings.

All rings are pendants.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f52d7c715ddfb07a0b78a97f02c56401452047b09dae892350835ad03e4fd91.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All rings can never be nails - False (Because, Some rings are nails).

II. Some beards are rings - False (Because, No definite relation given between beards and rings, so it can be possible only).

III. Some nails are pendants - True (Because, those part of nails that is ring is also pendants).

So, Only conclusion III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
